---
title: "ATO_CR: ATO Client Register"
description: "Demographic information about persons who have registered for an Australian Tax File Number with the ATO."
---

Demographic information about persons who have registered for an Australian Tax File Number with the ATO.

*Describes the Client Register as demographic information about people registered for a tax file number.*

The characters used are not published.","p":"1999 to current","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, Geocoding unit record data using address and location","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/statistical-geography/statistical-spatial-framework-ssf/statistical-spatial-framework-guidance-material/ssf-guidance-material-geocoding-unit-record-data-using-address-and-location","lim":"It does not certify that the mesh block on the row is present, only that the row belongs to the 2025 run, so an address can sit inside the run and still have no mesh block if the match failed. Comparing 2025 geography with a 2022 or 2023 table compares two index builds, not two locations.","where":["madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_25"]},{"n":"MB_ASGS_2021","d":"The finest geography on the ATO client register, giving the block of roughly 30 to 60 dwellings the client's address falls in.","full":"The finest geography on the ATO client register, giving the block of roughly 30 to 60 dwellings the client's address falls in. ABS defines them as \"the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS\", which \"form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)\", and there are 368,286 of them. It arrives only with the 2025 vintage of the address table, so mesh block geography is not available on the 2022, 2023 or 2024 extracts.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Mesh Blocks","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/mesh-blocks","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Mesh block coded to 2021 asgs","k":"ASGS 2021 Mesh Block code","def":"An eleven-digit ASGS Edition 3 mesh block code. ABS designs them around land use, so a block can be entirely commercial or a park, and two people in the same block are not co-resident. Because the column exists only on the 2025 table, any mesh block time series across ATO client register vintages has to be rebuilt from SA1 instead.","where":["madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_25"]},{"n":"POSTALTYPE","d":"Which kind of postal delivery point the address on this row is, such as a post office box, a locked bag or a roadside mail service.","full":"Which kind of postal delivery point the address on this row is, such as a post office box, a locked bag or a roadside mail service. It qualifies ADR_TYP beside it, which only says whether the address is residential or postal; this column says what sort of postal address it is. Australia Post warns that \"Often Postal Delivery Types are represented incorrectly making it difficult to match the address\", which is why the type is stored apart from the address text. It is empty on a residential address.","dsrc":"Australia Post, Barcode hints and tips, 'Postal Delivery Type' common address component abbreviations","durl":"https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/Barcode_hints_tips.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of postal address","k":"australia_post_postal_delivery_type","def":"Short upper case abbreviations from the Australia Post postal delivery type list, among them PO BOX, GPO BOX, LOCKED BAG, PRIVATE BAG, CARE PO, CMA, CMB, CPA, MS, RSD, RMB and RMS.","p":"1999 to current","s":"guessed","src":"Australia Post, 'Common address component abbreviations - Postal Delivery Type' (Barcode hints and tips)","lim":"A delivery point is not a place of residence. A rural taxpayer's post office box can sit in a town many kilometres from the property, so the SA1, SA2, SA4 and state columns on a row with a postal delivery type describe where the mail goes rather than where the person lives.","where":["madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_22","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_23","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_24","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_24_v2","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_25"],"dom":0},{"n":"SA1_ASGS_2021","d":"The small area of about 400 people that the client's address falls in, and the finest geography available on every vintage of the address table.","full":"The small area of about 400 people that the client's address falls in, and the finest geography available on every vintage of the address table. ABS defines SA1s as \"geographic areas built from whole Mesh Blocks\" and designs them to hold 200 to 800 people. Because ATO_CR carries SA1, SA2, SA4 and state but no SA3, an SA3 analysis has to be built up from this column through an ASGS correspondence.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Statistical Area Level 1","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-1","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sa1 location","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code","def":"An eleven-digit ASGS Edition 3 SA1 code. ABS defines SA2s as \"medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s)\" whose \"purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically\", generally holding 3,000 to 25,000 people. It is the level at which an ATO client register count can usually be compared with published population or income estimates without a correspondence.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Statistical Area Level 2","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sa2 location","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code","def":"A nine-digit ASGS Edition 3 SA2 code. It is also not nested inside the SA4 on the same row in any way a user needs to construct: both were assigned by the same coding run, so a mismatch between them signals a coding problem rather than a person straddling areas.","where":["madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_22","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_23","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_24","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_24_v2","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_25"]},{"n":"SA4_ASGS_2021","d":"The labour market region the client's address falls in, and the coarsest geography on the register below state.","full":"The labour market region the client's address falls in, and the coarsest geography on the register below state. ABS defines SA4s as \"geographic areas built from whole Statistical Areas Level 3 (SA3s)\" and states that \"SA4 boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively\". That makes it the right level for reading ATO client counts against Labour Force estimates, which are published on the same regions.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Statistical Area Level 4","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-4","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sa4 location","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 4 code","def":"A three-digit ASGS Edition 3 SA4 code. It sits on the dated demographics record with START_DATE and END_DATE, so a change is a new episode rather than an overwrite and the register can show a person's recorded sex changing over time. ABS describes the register as \"demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number\".","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida/plida-data-and-legislation","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Sex","k":"Sex as recorded on the ATO client register","def":"A short sex code with no published list. On an address row it opens an address episode; on a demographics row it opens a version of the client's details, so its subject differs between the address and demographics tables even though the name does not. The earliest dates run back to 1999, well before the 2006 start ABS gives for the register in PLIDA.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida/plida-data-and-legislation","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Start date","k":"Episode start date","def":"A calendar date. Episodes are intended to be contiguous within a client, so a gap between one END_DATE and the next START_DATE is a period with no record rather than a period living nowhere.","p":"1999 to current","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida/plida-data-and-legislation","lim":"It records when the ATO began using the record, not when the change happened. A person who moved in March and told the ATO in October gets an October start, so durations built from this column measure notification lags as well as residence, and comparing it against a Census night address will show apparent moves that are only reporting delays.","where":["madipge-ato-d-clientreg-demogs-1999-current / ato_cr_demogs_1999_22","madipge-ato-d-clientreg-demogs-1999-current / ato_cr_demogs_1999_23","madipge-ato-d-clientreg-demogs-1999-current / ato_cr_demogs_1999_24","madipge-ato-d-clientreg-demogs-1999-current / ato_cr_demogs_1999_25","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_22","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_23","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_24","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_24_v2","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_25"]},{"n":"STATE_ASGS_2021","d":"The state or territory the client's address falls in, held as an ASGS number rather than an abbreviation.","full":"The state or territory the client's address falls in, held as an ASGS number rather than an abbreviation. It is derived from the same address coding run as the SA1, SA2 and SA4 on the row, and ABS warns that these are \"a cartographic representation of legally designated boundaries and therefore should not be used for legal purposes\".","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Australia and State/Territory","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/australia-and-stateterritory","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"State (number)","k":"ASGS 2021 State and Territory code (1 to 9)","def":"A single digit from 1 to 9 under ASGS Edition 3. It matters most for addresses with sub-dwellings, where a unit in a block may code to the building rather than to the unit, and the ABS guidance asks that the degree to which a reported address matched the index record be kept with the geocode. Read the two flags together: FLAG says which outcome, this says how exact.","dsrc":"ABS, Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, Geocoding unit record data using address and location","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/statistical-geography/statistical-spatial-framework-ssf/statistical-spatial-framework-guidance-material/ssf-guidance-material-geocoding-unit-record-data-using-address-and-location","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Address coding sub flag","k":"Address geocoding sub-match flag","def":"A short secondary coding flag written by the ABS address coding run. It also does not say what was imprecise: a unit coded to its building and an address coded to a nearby locality centroid are both imprecise, and only one of them will put the person in a different SA1.","where":["madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_22","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_23","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_24","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_24_v2","madipge-ato-d-clientregaddr-1999-current / ato_cr_addr_1999_25"]},{"n":"SYNTHETIC_AEUID","d":"The person key that joins the client register's address history to its demographics and to the rest of PLIDA.","full":"The person key that joins the client register's address history to its demographics and to the rest of PLIDA. It is the reason the register is useful at all: on its own it holds no income, but as the ATO's roll of everyone with a tax file number it supplies a denominator that tax returns and payment summaries can be counted against. It is not a tax file number, an ATO client identifier or an ABN, so it can be matched across products but not decoded.","p":"1999 to current","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida/plida-data-and-legislation","lim":"It identifies a person only where the ATO record linked to the person spine, so a client who did not link is missing rather than absent from the tax system.
